ident: You're listening to Dale FM, music and company for the whole valley.
Dale FM. The friendly voice of the farms, the villages and everything in between.
This is Dale FM, and you're in good company.
Dale FM, easy listening for the long way round.
Still with me on Dale FM? Good. There's plenty more to come.
Hello again, and welcome back to Dale FM.
weather: A look at the weather. Cloud thickening from the west this afternoon, with a few spots of rain on the tops by teatime. Light winds, and a mild evening to follow.
The forecast for the dale. A bright start, a few showers through the middle of the day, and some good sunny spells in between. Take a coat, just in case.
Frost first thing on the higher ground, so mind the lanes. It should lift by mid morning, leaving a dry, cold, bright day.
Mist in the valley bottoms to begin with, clearing slowly. Then a grey, quiet afternoon with the wind picking up a little after dark.
It's turning wet across the moor this evening. Heavy rain at times, and the becks will be running fast by morning, so keep clear of the fords.
A breezy one today. Gusts of forty miles an hour on the tops, easing overnight. Good drying weather for the washing, not so good for the hay.
Fog patches again on the low roads tonight, and a touch of frost. Go gently if you're out and about.
Dry and bright for most of us tomorrow, with a cool north wind. A good day to get the outside jobs finished.
farming: Time for the farming report. Store lambs were steady at the market this week, with the best of the heavy lambs making a little more than last time.
Over to the farming desk. Barley is a touch firmer, wheat is quiet, and red diesel is down a few pence a litre on last month.
At the mart this week, a good show of cattle, with the prime beasts holding their price. Cull cows were a little cheaper.
A reminder for the farms. If you've got stock out on the high pasture, check the water troughs before the frost sets in.
This week on the Farming Hour, a few tips for the winter. Check your gates, check your fences, and check the oil in the tractor before the cold gets at it.
Hay and straw are in short supply across the dale, so if you've got a spare bale or two, there are folk who'd be glad of them.
The sheep dog trials are coming up this weekend at the show field. Entries close on Friday, and there will be tea and cake.
And a word on slurry. Spreading is now closed until the new year, so please keep to the dates and keep clear of the becks.
Ewes are looking well on the whole, but it's worth a second look at their feet before the ground gets wet. Foot rot waits for no one.
The tractor run for the hospice raises money again this year. Polish up your old Fergie, and meet at the green at ten.
news: This is the news from Dale FM. A fall in the price of red diesel has been welcomed by farmers across the county.
In local news, work to repair the bridge at the bottom of the dale will begin next week, and the road will be closed for around three weeks.
Councillors have approved plans for a new community shop in the village, which will open in the spring.
The parish council has appealed to drivers to slow down on the narrow lanes near the school, after several near misses this month.
A tractor and trailer blocked the main road for an hour this morning after losing a wheel. Nobody was hurt, and the road has now reopened.
The village hall has been awarded a grant to replace its roof, after volunteers raised more than eight thousand pounds.
Police are asking farmers to keep a close eye on fuel tanks and tools, after a number of thefts from yards in the area.
And finally, a prize marrow weighing more than forty kilos has taken first place at the village show. The grower says it was all in the soil.
The bus service between the market town and the villages will run a reduced timetable over the winter. Details are on the parish noticeboard.
A new walking route along the old railway line has opened, and walkers are asked to keep dogs on leads near the sheep.
That's the news. There's more at the top of the hour, and now back to the music.
The county show has announced the dates for next summer, and the organisers are already looking for volunteers.
Heavy rain overnight has left some of the low fields under water. The farmers affected say they have seen worse, but not recently.
A local cheesemaker has won a national award for a farmhouse cheddar. Orders are already coming in from as far as London.
phonein: And on the line we have Margaret, who says she's lost her best glove somewhere between the church and the chip shop. If you've seen a green one, give us a ring.
Our next caller is Dennis, who wants to tell us the swallows have left the barn early this year. He says that means a hard winter. We'll see.
We've had a message from a listener with a spare tractor seat. If you need one, it's in good condition, and it's yours for a cup of tea.
Someone has written in to ask about the strange noise on the top road last night. We think it was a tawny owl. We hope it was a tawny owl.
Barbara rang in to say thank you to whoever mended her gate. She says she would like to say thanks properly, with a fruit cake.
A caller is asking if anyone has seen a black and white collie wearing a red collar. She answers to Meg, and she's friendly.
John from the far end of the dale says his first snowdrops are out. That is early, even for him.
Our lines are open. Tell us your favourite song for a long drive, and we'll see what we can do.
traffic: On the roads, it's all clear on the main route into town. There's a tractor on the bend by the church, so allow a little extra time.
A word for drivers. The ford at the bottom of the lane is running high, so please use the bridge.
Sheep on the road near the top farm. Slow down, and give them room.
Roadworks with temporary lights on the valley road. Expect delays of about ten minutes.
Slippery conditions on the minor roads this evening, with mud from the fields. Take it steady.
The market town car park is full, so you might want to try the one by the river.
link: Stay with us. We've got plenty more for you.
That's a nice one. Let's keep it going.

ident: This is Quarry Rock. Turn it up.
You're locked on to Quarry Rock, the loudest station in the county.
Quarry Rock. Real music, no messing about.
Quarry Rock, and it's about to get louder.
Don't touch that dial. This is Quarry Rock.
Welcome back to Quarry Rock, where the riffs never stop.
weather: Weather time. It's grey, it's wet, and it's going to stay that way. Bring a hat.
Cold and clear tonight, with a hard frost by morning. Perfect weather for staying in and turning the volume up.
Wind and rain on the tops this afternoon, with gusts that will knock your hat off. It eases tomorrow.
Bright and breezy tomorrow, with sunshine for most of the day. A good one for the bike.
Thick fog on the low roads tonight, so slow down. You'll be glad you did.
Showers all day, some of them heavy. But there's a rainbow in there somewhere, I'm told.
A cold front is sweeping in from the north. Expect a sharp drop in temperature, and a few flurries of sleet on the high ground.
A dry spell at last. Make the most of it before the weekend wet arrives.
traffic: Traffic news. The bypass is moving slowly after a lorry shed its load of gravel. Take the back road if you can.
All quiet on the valley road, but there's a tractor in front of you on the long hill. Be patient.
A herd of cattle is crossing the lane by the quarry gates. They're not in a hurry, so you shouldn't be either.
Road closed at the bridge for repairs. Use the diversion past the old mill.
Oil on the road at the crossroads. Take care on the bend.
Fast and slippery on the top road tonight. If you're out on two wheels, treat it with respect.
gig: Gig guide. The Rusty Gates play the Black Horse on Friday night, and tickets are a fiver on the door.
On Saturday, a night of loud guitars at the village hall, with three bands and a bar. Doors at seven.
Local band The Slurry Pits are back for one night only, at the farmers' club. Bring earplugs.
The young farmers are putting on a barn dance with a rock band. Wellies are not optional.
A new rock night starts on Thursday at the pub in the market town. Open mic, and anyone can have a go.
Festival tickets go on sale this weekend, and they're not expected to last.
news: This is the news on Quarry Rock. A fall in the price of red diesel has been welcomed by farmers across the county.
Work to repair the bridge at the bottom of the dale will begin next week. The road will be closed for around three weeks.
Police are asking farmers to keep a close eye on their fuel tanks and tools after a number of thefts from yards in the area.
A tractor and trailer blocked the main road for an hour this morning after losing a wheel. Nobody was hurt.
A teenager from the village has won a place at the national championships for motocross. Friends say she has been practising every evening.
The council is asking drivers to slow down on the narrow lanes near the school, after a number of near misses.
The old quarry will host a charity rally next month, with proceeds going to the air ambulance.
Heavy rain overnight has flooded some of the low fields. Farmers say they have seen worse, but not recently.
A lorry has overturned on the long hill, spilling a load of bagged compost. The road is open again, but the verge is a mess.
That's the news. Now, back to the music.
A sheep has been rescued from a ledge on the quarry face after a two hour operation. The sheep is said to be unimpressed.
The county show organisers say next summer's event will be the biggest yet, with a new arena for the tractor pulling.
competition: Competition time. Answer this and win a pair of tickets. Which band made the song we just played? Ring in with your answer.
Our caller today wins a Quarry Rock mug and a box of vinyl. Question: how many strings has a bass guitar usually got?
It's the Name That Riff competition. I'll play a few notes, and the first person to ring in with the right answer wins a prize.
Win a pair of tickets to the festival. All you have to do is tell us what you would play at maximum volume.
The prize this week is a signed guitar pick, and a pie from the pub. Phone lines open now.
Today's mystery sound: we'll play it twice. The first caller to name it wins the lot.
phonein: Next caller, Steve, from the farm on the hill. He says his tractor radio only picks up us, and the cows prefer us to anything else.
A message from Kim, who says she's playing us loud enough that the neighbours are asking what the song is. Happy to help, Kim.
We've got Phil on the line. He says the best song to drive a quad bike to is anything with a big drum sound. I'd have to agree.
Dave rang in to request something with a lot of guitar, as he's been stuck in a tractor all day. Dave, we've got you.
Someone has asked us to turn it up. We already have.
A caller says she can hear us from the other side of the hill. We take that as a compliment.
link: Stay tuned. It only gets louder.
